caption: The drawing displays a rectangular, elaborately carved wooden mantle clock with a reddish-brown tone. At the top of the clock, there are decorative carvings featuring two mirrored birds with wings partially open and intricate leaf motifs. The main face of the clock is circular, located in the upper center section, and bordered by an orange and yellow pattern at each corner. The face is white with black Arabic numerals from 1 to 12, black clock hands, and an inscription with calligraphic text that reads: “Bishop & Bradley, 9 Court St, Watertown.” Inside the main dial is a smaller secondary dial, and both dials have pointer hands. Below the main clock face, in a rectangular panel, there is a colorful, symmetrical illustration featuring a portrait of a man surrounded by American flags, a pair of crossed cannons, drumsticks, and decorative foliage. Above the portrait, there is a golden eagle with spread wings, with a shield and a circle motif between the wings. The outer frame of the clock is designed with vertical carved patterns and floral elements, matching the color and style of the top section. The background of the image is plain and cream-colored, and there is a handwritten signature at the lower right of the clock that reads “Leo. W. Jansen 1935.”
title: Clock, Eight Day
